newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says to help wind up Osaka credit union.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says to help wind up Osaka credit union.

text.p: Japan's Finance Ministry said on Friday it would cooperate with the Osaka prefectural government in winding up the business of Sanpuku Shinyo Kumiai, a small credit union in Osaka.

"Early disposal of bad loans held by financial institutions is an urgent task for the sake of the Japanese economy. We believe that dealing with failed financial institutions without any delay will lead to the rejuvenation of the functions of Japan's financial system," MOF said in a statement.
The statement was issued after the Osaka prefectural government ordered a partial suspension of Sanpuku's business.
The prefectural government said its investigations showed that Sanpuku had made false reports about its outstanding loans to cover up the deterioration of its assets.
The prefectural government will work out a plan to wind up the credit union, aiming to transfer all of Sanpuku's business to the Resolution and Collection Bank Ltd.
The body was set up in September to handle the bankruptcies of credit unions and deal with possible future failures of such financial institutions.
"We will extend our cooperation in working out a full-fledged plan to wind up the credit union with the aim of transferring Sanpuku's business to the Bank," the ministry said.
MOF said the National Federation of Credit Cooperatives is expected to provide funds to Sanpuku if the credit union has a run on deposits and cannot return customers' funds.
An Osaka government official said Sanpuku has total assets of 33.9 billion yen, of which unrecoverable loans total 7.7 billion yen.
